title: Exceptional point induced by hyperbolicity in an electrostatic spherical shell
authors: Álvaro Buendía, Marcelo S. Barreiro, Nuno M. R. Peres
abstract: Exceptional points (EPs) are non--Hermitian degeneracies at which both eigenvalues and eigenvectors coalesce, usually engineered through balanced gain and loss or non--reciprocity. In this work, we show that the radial electrostatic problem of an anisotropic core--shell nanoparticle realizes an EP without any of the alluded conditons. Written in the logarithmic radial coordinate, the problem is a Cauchy--Euler equation that maps onto a damped oscillator and, equivalently, onto a two-site Hatano--Nelson Hamiltonian, so that the non-Hermiticity is emulated in space rather than in time and the sole control parameter is the degree of dielectric anisotropy, $\varepsilon_t/\varepsilon_r$. The shell is passive, reciprocal, and lossless, yet it hosts an EP and a non--Hermitian phase transition governed by hyperbolicity alone. Beyond a hyperbolicity threshold the electric field inside the shell turns from monotonic decay into spatial oscillation, producing hotspots at intermediate radii which can be exploited to tailor fluorescence, strong coupling, sensing, or cloaking. More broadly, this establishes hyperbolic media as a platform to simulate non--Hermitian physics without gain, loss, or non--reciprocity.
summary: This work shows that an electrostatic spherical shell can host an exceptional point (EP) and exhibit non-Hermitian physics solely by exploiting dielectric anisotropy, without needing gain or loss. By mapping the radial problem to a damped oscillator, the authors demonstrate that crossing a hyperbolicity threshold causes the internal electric field to switch from decaying to oscillating. This establishes hyperbolic media as a powerful, passive platform for simulating non-Hermitian phenomena.
main_problem: The paper demonstrates that an exceptional point (EP) and non-Hermitian phase transition can be realized in a passive, reciprocal, and lossless electrostatic spherical shell using only dielectric anisotropy.
main_result: Hyperbolic media provide a platform to simulate non-Hermitian physics, causing the internal electric field to transition from monotonic decay to spatial oscillation across the EP.
method: The problem is reduced to solving a Cauchy-Euler equation in the logarithmic radial coordinate, which maps onto a damped oscillator and a two-site Hatano-Nelson Hamiltonian.
model_or_system: The system is an anisotropic core-shell nanoparticle where the permittivity tensor in the shell is diagonal, $\epsilon_b = 	ext{diag}(\epsilon_r, \epsilon_t, \epsilon_t)$. The physics is governed by the dielectric anisotropy factor, $\epsilon_t/\epsilon_r$.
key_observables: Electric field amplitude $|E|/E_0$, field localization in the $	heta$ parameter, and the appearance of anomalous secular modes at the EP.
important_parameters: The dielectric anisotropy factor $\epsilon_t/\epsilon_r$ acts as the sole control parameter, defining regimes like elliptic, hyperbolic overdamped, and hyperbolic underdamped.
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to the dipolar term ($l=1$) in the initial notes, and the general framework uses separation of variables for the electrostatic potential.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the physical setup, the phase diagram of field exponents vs. anisotropy, and cross-sections of the field amplitude $|E|/E_0$ showing the transition across the EP for different anisotropy values.
paper_structure: The paper analyzes the electrostatic potential using separation of variables, deriving a Cauchy-Euler equation. It then maps this equation to known non-Hermitian models (damped oscillator, Hatano-Nelson) to analyze the transition controlled by the anisotropy parameter.
why_interesting: The ability to engineer non-Hermitian physics (like EPs) using purely classical, passive electromagnetic boundary conditions (hyperbolicity) is highly relevant for designing novel metamaterials and optical devices.
